sources.entry: BOLT: A Practical Binary Optimizer for Data Centers and Beyond - States why a profile applied to the final binary beats one mapped to source, and the layout passes accuracy enables.

summary.title: BOLT: A Practical Binary Optimizer for Data Centers and Beyond
summary.one_liner: BOLT is a post-link binary optimizer built on LLVM that uses sample-based profiles to improve code layout, giving speedups on top of FDO and LTO.
keywords: how to speed up a compiled binary after linking
takeaways: Post-link optimization on the final binary can improve code layout even when FDO and LTO are already applied.
BOLT uses sample-based profiling and is built on the LLVM framework.
Reported results: up to 8.0% speedup over profile-guided function reordering and LTO on Facebook data-center workloads.
Reported results: up to 20.4% speedup for GCC and Clang on top of FDO and LTO, and up to 52.1% without FDO and LTO.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (Rafael Auler et al., 2018) presents BOLT, a post-link optimizer built on LLVM that reorders code in an already-linked binary using sample-based profiles. The authors argue code layout matters for large data-center applications and that post-link improvements are complementary to compiler-level FDO and whole-program LTO. They evaluate on Facebook data-center workloads and on GCC and Clang binaries, reporting the speedups listed above. The listing note highlights the argument that a profile mapped to the final binary can beat one mapped back to source. The page itself is only the abstract and metadata, so details of the layout passes are not in the page text.
